entities.name: Indian borrowers (ECB and trade credit)
entities.profile: Companies, LLPs and other non-individual residents raising ECB or trade credit, or borrowing from non-residents.

entities.name: NBFCs and HFCs
entities.profile: RBI-regulated NBFCs and housing finance companies borrowing abroad or lending to non-residents.

entities.name: Lenders to non-residents or abroad
entities.profile: Residents lending to non-residents in India or to their foreign entities, and non-resident lenders to Indian borrowers.

entities.name: Parties to cross-border guarantees
entities.profile: Resident sureties, principal debtors and creditors in guarantees with a non-resident party.

entities.name: AD Category-I banks
entities.profile: Banks that act as designated AD for ECB, trade credit, guarantees and hedging.

updates.title: Export and Import of Goods and Services (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2026
updates.applies: Exporters and importers of services, and authorised dealer banks.
changes: In force from 01-10-2026. A new definition of "resident individual" is added.

A service exporter is treated as having filed the Export Declaration Form on giving the receipt details to the bank: this applies to resident individuals, and to others where the inward remittance is up to ₹10 lakh.
For service imports, the bank enters details in the import monitoring system (IDPMS) only for non-individual importers with an invoice or contract above ₹10 lakh, within five working days.
RBI issued a press release and FAQs on the new trade regulations on 20-11-2026.

borrower.text: Less paperwork for small service exports and imports.

adbank.text: Update export and import monitoring workflows.

nbfc.text: No change to borrowing or lending rules.

actions: Authorised dealer banks: update EDF and IDPMS processes for services.

updates.title: Compounding of certain FEMA contraventions delegated to RBI Regional Offices
updates.applies: Applicants compounding contraventions of the Borrowing and Lending Regulations, the Guarantees Regulations or the overseas investment framework.
changes: Borrowing and lending, and guarantee, contraventions are compounded by the Regional Office with jurisdiction over the applicant's registered office.
Overseas investment cases go to one of seven Regional Offices by the prefix of the unique identification number; mixed cases stay with the Central Office.

borrower.text: File compounding applications with the right Regional Office.

actions: Check which RBI office should receive any pending or planned compounding application.

updates.title: Non-deliverable rupee derivatives for non-residents only for hedging; reserve on AD banks' own hedges
updates.applies: AD banks with IFSC banking units, standalone primary dealers, and non-resident users.
changes: AD banks may offer non-deliverable rupee derivatives to non-residents only for hedging.
A 20% Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve applies to AD banks' own rupee hedges where they buy foreign currency.

adbank.text: Change product approval for non-resident NDDCs and fund the reserve on own hedges.

lender.text: Non-resident lenders hedging rupee ECBs through NDDCs must show a hedging purpose.

actions: Update hedging documentation for non-resident users.

updates.title: Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve of 20% on rupee derivatives hedging current account payments
updates.applies: AD banks and users buying foreign currency forward against rupees for current account transactions.
changes: AD banks keep 20% of the rupee notional of each such contract above USD 2 million as cash with RBI until the contract ends.
Splitting deals to stay below the threshold is a violation.

adbank.text: Daily reserve with RBI and CIMS reporting.

borrower.text: Hedging costs for import payments, including trade credit, may rise.

actions: Expect revised pricing on forward cover above USD 2 million.

updates.title: No rebooking of cancelled rupee derivatives; threshold without proof of exposure cut to USD 5 million
updates.applies: Users hedging with AD banks, including ECB and trade credit borrowers, and AD banks.
changes: Cancelled rupee derivatives may not be rebooked; rollovers on maturity are still allowed.
Positions without establishing the underlying exposure fall from USD 100 million to USD 5 million.
Users give an undertaking that the same exposure is not hedged with another AD bank.

borrower.text: Hedge decisions on ECB and trade credit can no longer be undone and redone freely.

adbank.text: Collect undertakings and keep documents for two years.

actions: Review hedging policy for ECB and trade credit exposures.
Keep evidence of the underlying exposure ready.

updates.title: Seven old FEMA circulars withdrawn, including ECB circulars on rupee bonds and rupee ECB
updates.applies: AD banks and borrowers relying on older ECB circulars.
changes: Withdrawn: ECB circulars on rupee denominated bonds overseas (2015), ECB in Indian rupees (2014), the infrastructure definition (2014), tax-free bonds bought by non-residents (2013), import of services (2013) and ECB by SIDBI (2012), plus one MTSS circular.

borrower.text: Rely on the 2026 ECB framework, not the withdrawn circulars.

updates.title: Deposit (Sixth Amendment) Regulations, 2026: SNRR accounts for any non-resident, including in IFSC
updates.applies: Non-residents doing rupee business in India, and AD banks.
changes: Any person resident outside India may open an SNRR account with an AD bank in India or its branch outside India, including in an IFSC.
Transfers between NRO and NRE or SNRR accounts within the Remittance of Assets limit are allowed.

lender.text: Non-resident lenders have a wider rupee account option.

updates.title: Daily reporting of ECBs raised under RBI's swap facility
updates.applies: AD banks handling ECBs, FCNR(B) deposits and overseas foreign currency borrowings mobilised under RBI's June 2026 swap facility.
changes: Daily data by 6 p.m., with a nil statement on days with no transactions.

borrower.text: Borrowers using the swap facility should expect information requests from their AD bank.

updates.title: AD banks barred from rupee derivatives with related parties, with exceptions
updates.applies: AD banks and their related parties.
changes: Replaces the 1 April 2026 instructions.
No rupee derivatives with related parties, except cancellation and rollover of existing contracts and back-to-back deals with unrelated non-resident users.

updates.title: FPI debt limits for 2026-27; corporate bond limit stays at 15%
updates.applies: Issuers of bonds and NCDs bought by FPIs, FPIs and custodians.
changes: Corporate bond limit: Rs 9,36,113 crore for April-September 2026 and Rs 9,91,392 crore for October 2026-March 2027.
Voluntary Retention Route investments come under the General Route limits from 01-04-2026.

borrower.text: More headroom for FPI subscription to corporate bonds.

updates.title: Overseas investment references to RBI moved to seven Regional Offices
updates.applies: Indian entities lending to or guaranteeing for foreign entities, and AD banks.
changes: References go through PRAVAAH to the Regional Office set by the UIN prefix (Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Mumbai, Kolkata, New Delhi, Hyderabad or Chennai).

lender.text: References for overseas lending go to the mapped Regional Office.

updates.title: Guarantee reporting forms GRN Issue, Modification and Invocation
updates.applies: Residents who must report cross-border guarantees, and AD banks.
changes: New GRN forms for issue, modification and invocation.
AD banks report on CIMS within 30 days of quarter-end and allot a Guarantee Transaction Number.
For the late fee, the amount is nil for issue and modification, and the surety's liability for invocation.

guarantee.text: Report guarantees in the new forms within 15 days of quarter-end.

borrower.text: Applies to guarantees securing ECB or trade credit.

nbfc.text: Applies where the NBFC is a principal debtor or creditor.

actions: Set up a quarterly guarantee reporting calendar.

updates.title: Late submission fee for ECB returns: per return, paid to the Regional Office
updates.applies: ECB borrowers and designated AD banks.
changes: Form ECB 1 and Revised Form ECB 1 are returns that do not capture flows for the fee.
Each late Form ECB 2 is a separate instance.
AD banks forward returns within 7 calendar days and monitor payment; the fee is paid to the RBI Regional Office after RBI's email.

borrower.text: Late monthly returns now cost a fee each.

adbank.text: Forward returns within 7 days and track fee payment.

actions: Diarise Form ECB 2 for the 7th calendar day of each month.

updates.title: New Form ECB 1 and Form ECB 2
updates.applies: ECB borrowers and designated AD banks.
changes: Form ECB 1 and Revised Form ECB 1 replace Form ECB; a new Form ECB 2 replaces the old return.

borrower.text: Use the new forms for every ECB.

updates.title: New ECB framework: Borrowing and Lending (First Amendment) Regulations, 2026
updates.applies: All resident non-individual borrowers, non-resident lenders and AD banks.
changes: Any non-individual resident incorporated or registered under a Central or State Act may borrow; any non-resident is a recognised lender.
Limit: higher of USD 1 billion outstanding or 300% of net worth, not applicable to entities regulated by a financial sector regulator.
Minimum average maturity of 3 years (1-3 years for manufacturers up to USD 150 million); cost at market terms.
A single end-use list in regulation 3A; RBI-regulated entities may not issue guarantees for ECBs.
ECBs registered earlier continue on their old terms except for reporting.

borrower.text: Wider access, new limit and maturity tests, new end-use list.

nbfc.text: No borrowing limit for regulated NBFCs, but end-use and on-lending restrictions apply; no NBFC guarantees for ECB.

actions: Recheck planned ECBs against the new limit, maturity and end-use rules.
Update loan documents for the security clause and NOC requirements.

updates.title: Voluntary Retention Route merged into the General Route from 01-04-2026
changes: FPI debt investment under the Voluntary Retention Route is governed by the General Route conditions from 01-04-2026.

borrower.text: Issuers should note the single route for FPI debt.

updates.title: Foreign Exchange Management (Guarantees) Regulations, 2026 in force
updates.applies: Residents who are sureties, principal debtors or creditors in guarantees with a non-resident party, and AD banks.
changes: Replace the Guarantees Regulations, 2000.
A resident may be surety or principal debtor if the underlying transaction is permitted and both are eligible to lend and borrow under the B&L Regulations.
Quarterly reporting within 15 days of quarter-end, and a late submission fee.
19 older guarantee circulars withdrawn.

guarantee.text: New eligibility test and reporting for every cross-border guarantee.

borrower.text: Guarantees securing ECB must meet the 2026 rules.

nbfc.text: RBI-regulated entities still may not guarantee ECBs.

actions: Map all existing cross-border guarantees and report them on the new basis.
